title: Inbound guard findings
intro: Findings are written by fixed rules running on this machine: Guaardvark's own, and any an extension adds (each finding says which). Quoted lines come from the change itself. The guard is in {{mode}} mode.
introGit: Findings are written by fixed rules running on this machine: Guaardvark's own, and any an extension adds (each finding says which). Quoted lines come from the change itself. The guard is in {{mode}} mode; the git hooks are in {{gitMode}} mode.

view.resolvedTooltip: What was approved, rejected or closed, with when, by whom and the note.

source.watch: found on disk by the sweep

ownDecision.chipTooltip: A finding here is a way off the machine: a network destination, a hosted service, a key or a secret. Approve all and Approve selected leave it out. It is approved only by opening it and typing a note.
ownDecision.alert: This change touches a way off the machine ({{rules}}). No batch approves it. To approve it, type a note in your own words below; the note is stored with the approval.
ownDecision.noteNeeded: Type a note saying why before approving: this change touches a way off the machine.

approveAllTooltip: Every row shown under this tab and these filters. Blocked rows are left out unless you tick them in the next step. Rows that touch a way off the machine are always left out.
rejectAllTooltip: Every row shown under this tab and these filters that can be rejected. Git records cannot be rejected here; they are left out.
rejectSelectedTooltip: Git records cannot be rejected here; they are left out.
howToSelect: Click a row to read it. Tick its box or Ctrl/Cmd-click to select it; Shift-click selects a range.
sizeWholeTooltip: The sweep reads each file whole: {{files}} file(s), {{lines}} line(s)
emptyFiltered: Nothing under this tab and these filters.
clickRow: Click a row to read what the guard found.

detail.noCommitDates: Commit dates unknown: this record names no commits this clone has.
detail.noDate: No file or commit date for this kind of item.

decision.clearTooltip: Closed without a person: the guard found nothing, or the file changed or was removed afterwards.

result.leftForYou_one: {{count}} left for you: it touches a way off the machine. Open it and approve it on its own, with a note.
result.leftForYou_other: {{count}} left for you: they touch a way off the machine. Open each and approve it on its own, with a note.
result.cleared: Removed {{total}} decided records ({{rejected}} rejected, {{cleared}} closed). {{approved}} approvals and {{open}} open items were not touched.

confirm.approveText: Each item is approved on its own, in order, and gets its own approval record with your note. One that cannot be approved stays open, and the reason is shown.
confirm.approveNothing: Nothing here can be approved as a batch: every item is blocked or touches a way off the machine. Tick below to include the blocked ones, or cancel.
confirm.approveNothingOwn: Nothing here can be approved as a batch: every item touches a way off the machine. Open each one and approve it on its own, with a note.
confirm.rejectText: Each item is rejected on its own and gets its own record with your note. Git records are not in this list: they cannot be rejected here.
confirm.ownDecisionCount: {{count}} left out: approved one at a time, with a note
confirm.includeBlocks: Also approve the {{count}} blocked item(s). Read every finding first.
confirm.keepsShown: rows not shown under this tab or filter

history.clearTooltip: Remove rejected and closed records from this list for good. Approvals are kept.
history.clearNothing: Nothing to clear: only approvals and records still in use are left.
history.title: Clear the decided records?
history.text: Removes the rejected and closed records from this machine's database. A rejected change that comes in again is judged again from the start.
history.keeps: {{approved}} approvals (they are what lets the same change pass again), {{open}} open items, {{inUse}} decided records still in use (a pending fix or a file the sweep holds shows them), and the git ledger file with every approval made from the command line

finding.byUnknown: Rule (recorded before findings named their scanner; an extension scanner also ran)
